content.value_statement: Federal acquisition research can lose traceability across documents, sources, calculations, and decisions. This skill organizes a staged workflow with approvals, evidence IDs, and validated reports.
actual_capabilities: Guides users through quick research, complete reports, report refreshes, focused analysis, or pre-award handoff.
Registers supplied acquisition documents and identifies status, controlling sections, conflicts, gaps, and stale content.
Builds approval-based research plans with sanitized queries, approved providers, source scopes, and public URL allowlists.
Separates sourced facts, user statements, inferences, decisions, unresolved questions, and calculation evidence.
Generates structured FAR Part 10 DOCX reports from validated research records.
Validates report sections, evidence citations, approval gates, sensitive fields, public URLs, and numeric totals.
limitations: Complete reports require Python, python-docx, a DOCX renderer, approved web access, and relevant federal MCP capabilities.
The workflow does not make Contracting Officer determinations or final acquisition strategy decisions.
Without commercial evidence and web access, output remains a federal-data desk-research draft.
Users must review source quality, resolve document conflicts, and approve findings and decisions before final generation.

use_cases.title: Prepare a FAR Part 10 report
use_cases.description: Turn acquisition documents and approved research into a traceable, validated market research report.

use_cases.title: Analyze one acquisition question
use_cases.description: Compare evidence about competition, commerciality, vendors, pricing, or small-business availability without forcing a final decision.

use_cases.title: Refresh prior market research
use_cases.description: Review an existing report, identify stale evidence and conflicts, then update only affected research areas.

prompt_templates.title: Start quick research
prompt_templates.prompt: Conduct quick federal market research for [requirement]. Show findings in chat and ask for approval before using external sources.
prompt_templates.scenario: Begin a focused, lightweight research task.

prompt_templates.title: Build a complete report
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a FAR Part 10 market research report for [requirement]. I will provide acquisition documents, scope, identifiers, and known constraints.
prompt_templates.scenario: Create a formal report through the complete staged workflow.

prompt_templates.title: Refresh an existing report
prompt_templates.prompt: Refresh the attached market research report as of [date]. Preserve approved decisions, flag conflicts, and propose research only for stale or missing evidence.
prompt_templates.scenario: Update prior research while preserving document history and decision boundaries.

prompt_templates.title: Evaluate a decision area
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze [decision area] for [requirement]. Separate supporting evidence, contrary evidence, uncertainty, and permitted options without making the final acquisition decision.
prompt_templates.scenario: Produce advanced decision support for an authorized acquisition reviewer.

output_examples.input: Analyze small-business availability for a help desk services requirement.
output_examples.output: A findings register separates agency-specific and government-wide evidence, identifies data gaps, cites each source, and presents decision options for user approval.

output_examples.input: Refresh a two-year-old market research report using the attached documents.
output_examples.output: A document register identifies controlling and stale sections, a revised research plan covers affected topics, and unresolved precedence questions are presented before research.

output_examples.input: Create a complete FAR Part 10 report after findings and decisions are approved.
output_examples.output: A validated DOCX contains required sections, evidence citations, approved decisions, limitations, a reproducible search log, and independently checked calculations.

best_practices: Provide available acquisition documents before approving the research plan.
Use sanitized public terms and review every proposed provider, query, and extraction URL.
Approve findings, decisions, and unresolved-item dispositions explicitly before generating a formal report.
anti_patterns: Do not send procurement-sensitive, proprietary, controlled, classified, or source-selection content to public services.
Do not treat historical percentages or thin results as automatic acquisition decisions.
Do not call an incomplete desk-research draft a complete contract-file-ready report.

faq.question: Can this skill create a complete FAR Part 10 report?
faq.answer: Yes. Complete output requires approved research, sufficient federal and commercial evidence, approved decisions, and successful DOCX validation.

faq.question: Does the skill make acquisition decisions?
faq.answer: No. It presents evidence, uncertainty, and permitted options for the user or authorized Contracting Officer.

faq.question: Can I use it without web access?
faq.answer: Yes. Federal MCP data and supplied documents can support a desk-research draft, which must state missing source classes.

faq.question: How does it handle sensitive information?
faq.answer: It requires sanitized public queries, rejects credential-like fields and unsafe URLs, and prohibits uploading source documents to public providers.

faq.question: Can it update an existing report?
faq.answer: Yes. It registers existing documents, preserves approved status, flags conflicts, and proposes focused research for stale or missing evidence.

faq.question: What tools are needed for DOCX output?
faq.answer: Python 3, python-docx, and LibreOffice or an equivalent renderer are required for generation and layout validation.
